note.text: Commercial banks provide customer deposits, payments and credit, normally subject to banking rules and commercial constraints. A transfer within a bank reduces the sender’s deposit and increases the recipient’s deposit without itself increasing the combined balance. A new bank loan credited to a borrower’s account creates both a loan asset and a matching deposit liability. The bank still faces capital, liquidity, risk, profitability and settlement constraints. It does not create unlimited wealth or freely spend every customer liability as profit.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish moving existing deposits from creating a deposit through lending. Builds on: bank claims, payment services and risk. Leads to: balance-sheet entries and credit creation.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: A fictional Douala supplier receives a transfer from another customer at the same bank. Their combined balance is unchanged when no fees or lending occur. A separate loan credited by the bank increases a borrower’s deposit and debt together. A payment to another bank can require interbank settlement, which differs from merely relabelling balances within one bank.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the event: existing-balance transfer, new lending, principal repayment or fee. State the perspective and track both sides. Do not call every digital balance movement new money or assume a bank loan adds equal net wealth to its borrower.

cards.idea: Distinguish the monetary concepts before evaluating a case.
example: within-bank transfer: movement of an existing balance between customers of the same bank.
loan-created deposit: a deposit credited alongside a new bank loan claim.
interbank settlement: settlement of obligations between different banks.
commercial constraint: a risk or resource condition limiting bank decisions.

example: Sender loses the amount that recipient gains.
The bank records an asset and matching deposit liability.

cards.idea: Explain a consequence instead of assuming every option has the same effect.
example: within-bank transfer: Without new lending or fees, this transfer leaves the combined total unchanged.
loan-created deposit: The new loan is also an obligation of the borrower.
interbank settlement: They concern different holders and claims.
commercial constraint: Capital, liquidity, demand and risk still constrain lending.

questions.prompt: At an imaginary bank, account A holds {a} CFA francs and account B holds {b}. A transfers {x} to B within this same bank. No fees or new lending occur. What is their combined deposit balance afterwards?

misconceptions.explain: The transfer moves an existing deposit; it does not add this amount to the combined balance.
The recipient receives what the sender loses, so the combined balance does not shrink.

solution: A ends with {a-x}; B ends with {b+x}.
